intro.text: This entry describes an autosomal recessive form of severe congenital neutropenia, designated SCN14. The causal gene and the reports that defined this form cannot be stated here with confidence.

checks.claim: SCN14 is an autosomal recessive form of severe congenital neutropenia.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results suggest that CSF3 deficiency in humans causes a novel autosomal recessive form of SCN.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a novel autosomal recessive form of SCN caused by CSF3 deficiency, but it never uses the designation 'SCN14'.

paragraphs.text: Severe congenital neutropenia (SCN) is a genetically heterogeneous group of bone marrow failure disorders. They are defined by very low absolute neutrophil counts from early life, usually with maturation arrest of myelopoiesis at the promyelocyte/myelocyte stage in the bone marrow. Affected individuals have recurrent, often life-threatening bacterial infections starting in infancy. SCN14 is an autosomal recessive form of the disorder.
